events.title_en: Final break between Eastern and Western churches
events.description_en: In 1054 the pope's representative excommunicated the patriarch of Constantinople, who cursed the pope in return. The split led to the Eastern Orthodox Churches and the division between Roman Catholicism and Eastern Orthodoxy.

events.title_en: Luther posts his 95 theses — start of the Protestant Reformation
events.title_ta: புராட்டஸ்டன்டு சீர்திருத்த இயக்கம் 1517-ம் ஆண்டு அக்டோபர் 31-ல் அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாக தொடங்கியதென்று சொல்லலாம்
events.description_en: Indignant at John Tetzel's sale of indulgences, Martin Luther, according to tradition, nailed 95 theses to the castle church door at Wittenberg on October 31, 1517. Printed and spread widely, they made church reform a Europe-wide controversy.

events.title_en: Erasmus: "The shamelessness of the Roman Curia has reached its climax"
events.description_en: In 1518, amid papal corruption, Catholic scholar Erasmus wrote that the shamelessness of the Roman Curia had reached its climax.

sources.quote_en: It was with full justification that the Dutch Catholic scholar Erasmus wrote in 1518: “The shamelessness of the Roman Curia has reached its climax.”

events.title_en: Zwingli begins preaching reform in Zurich
events.description_en: Around 1519, Catholic priest Ulrich (Huldrych) Zwingli, then living in Zurich, began preaching against indulgences, Mariolatry, clerical celibacy, and other Catholic doctrines.
events.description_ta: சுமார் 1519-ல் பாவ மன்னிப்பு, மரியாள் வழிபாடு, குருமார் மணத்துறவு போன்ற இன்னும் பிற கத்தோலிக்க சர்ச்சின் கோட்பாடுகளையெல்லாம் தாக்கி ஸ்விங்லி பிரச்சாரம் செய்ய ஆரம்பித்தார்.

events.description_en: On June 15, 1520, Pope Leo X issued a bull ordering that no book containing "heresies" be printed, sold, or read in any Catholic land.

sources.quote_en: On June 15, 1520, Pope Leo X had issued a bull ordering that no book containing “heresies” be printed, sold, or read in any Catholic land and demanding that the secular authorities enforce the bull within their domains.

events.description_en: In 1522, after the clergy moved against practices contrary to church doctrine, Zwingli was charged with heresy and resigned from the Catholic priesthood.

events.title_en: Carey moves his press to Serampore
events.description_en: During 1800 Carey transferred his printing establishment to the Danish settlement at Serampore, where many Bible translations were printed (over 212,000 volumes between 1801 and 1832).

sources.title_en: Translating the Bible in India
sources.quote_en: At first, local people referred to the press as the ‘god whom the English worship.’ During 1800 Carey transferred his printing establishment to the more hospitable Danish settlement at Serampore.

events.title_en: Mary Jones walks 25 miles for a Welsh Bible
events.title_ta: 1800-ல், மேரி ஒரு பாதிரியாரிடமிருந்து வேல்ஸ் மொழியில் பைபிளை வாங்குவதற்காக வெறுங்காலோடு 40 கிலோமீட்டர் நடந்து சென்றாள்
events.description_en: In 1800, 16-year-old Mary Jones walked barefoot 25 miles to buy a Welsh Bible. The clergyman who helped her later discussed the need for Bibles with friends in London, leading to the British and Foreign Bible Society.
events.description_ta: 1800-ல், மேரி ஒரு பாதிரியாரிடமிருந்து வேல்ஸ் மொழியில் பைபிளை வாங்குவதற்காக வெறுங்காலோடு 40 கிலோமீட்டர் நடந்து சென்றாள்.

sources.title_en: Part Three—How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: In 1800, Mary walked barefoot for 25 miles [40 km] to buy a Welsh Bible from a clergyman.

events.title_en: Bible available in about 70 languages

events.title_en: British and Foreign Bible Society founded
events.title_ta: 81 பிரிட்டிஷ் அண்ட் ஃபாரின் பைபிள் சொஸைட்டி 1804-ல் நிறுவப்பட்டது
events.description_en: The British and Foreign Bible Society was formed in London in 1804 to provide affordable Bibles in people's own languages "without note or comment." It triggered the founding of many other Bible societies.
events.description_ta: இதன் விளைவாக 1804-ல் பிரிட்டிஷ் அண்ட் ஃபாரின் பைபிள் சொஸைட்டி தோன்றியது.

events.title_en: Robert Morrison arrives in China to translate the Bible

events.description_en: In 1807, 25-year-old Robert Morrison sailed to China, where teaching the language to foreigners was a capital offense, and secretly worked on a Chinese Bible.

events.title_en: Entire Bible in Bengali issued

events.title_en: Fire at Serampore destroys unpublished translations
events.description_en: In 1812 a fire at the Serampore press destroyed several unpublished Bible translations, including a Telugu one; Carey quickly reorganized printing.

sources.title_en: Translating the Bible in India
sources.quote_en: Then came a setback in 1812, when a fire at the Serampore press destroyed several painstakingly made, unpublished Bible translations.

events.title_en: Associate Bible societies formed in Germany, Netherlands, Denmark, and Russia
events.description_en: By 1813 associate societies had been formed in Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and Russia. Lacking translators of Hebrew and Greek, many translations sponsored by the British and Foreign Bible Society were based on the King James Version.
events.description_ta: ஆரம்பகால உற்சாகம் வேகமாக பரவ, 1813-க்குள் துணை சங்கங்கள் ஜெர்மனியிலும் நெதர்லாந்திலும் டென்மார்க்கிலும் ரஷ்யாவிலும் தோன்றியிருந்தன.

sources.title_en: Part Three—How the Bible Came to Us

events.description_en: Adoniram Judson began translating the Bible into Burmese in 1817, a task that took some 18 years.

events.title_en: Morrison completes the entire Bible in Chinese

events.title_en: Judson completes Burmese Christian Greek Scriptures

sources.title_en: Part Three—How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: BURMA, 1824—The king’s officers have just ransacked Adoniram and Ann Judson’s missionary home, taking everything they thought valuable.

sources.title_en: They Loved the Word of God
sources.quote_en: Fearing that buried under the house the manuscript might be destroyed by humidity and mildew, Ann sewed it inside a pillow and brought it to her husband in prison.

events.title_en: Moffat prints Gospel of Luke in Tswana

events.title_en: Malayalam Bible published, using "Jehovah"

events.title_en: Millerites' "Great Disappointment"
events.description_en: William Miller predicted Christ's visible return in 1843 or 1844. Some 50,000 Millerites waited on October 22, 1844, and when Christ did not come they called it the "Great Disappointment."
